text: Theo writes one Terraform root module declaring both the azurerm and aws providers, with remote state locked on Azure Storage. One shared project, one plan-and-apply cycle, covering both clouds at once — state locking matters even more here, with twice the blast radius if it's skipped.

An AKS module provisions the exact cluster shape Lesson 4 built by hand with the Azure CLI — now expressed as code that can be planned, reviewed, and reapplied consistently. An AWS backup module provisions the cross-region-replicated storage bucket and standby database replica from Lesson 3's architecture.

The real point of one shared project is that the architecture diagram stops being just a picture. A terraform plan surfaces drift on either cloud in the same review — nobody can quietly resize the AWS backup database without it showing up alongside any AKS change.

Not everything is codified yet, and that's deliberate: Kubernetes objects like Deployments and HPAs stay as plain kubectl YAML, and the FinOps dashboard Lesson 7 builds goes straight into Grafana, not Terraform — both decisions made to keep iteration fast this close to the sale.
